correctness.rationale: The direct \(2\times2\) orthogonal projection calculation gives \(E_\theta=1/(\cos^2(\phi-\theta)+\varepsilon^2\sin^2(\phi-\theta))\). A uniform Gaussian projective angle turns the simultaneous threshold into the exact intersection of arcs and proves the CDF and maximal atom. Integrating the distance to the swept orthogonality arc proves the expected supremum and eps-downarrow-zero asymptotics. Independence and AM-GM prove the segment product and equal-length optimizer. Strict \(f\prime\prime(k)=-u^2/[k(1-u)^2]<0\), derivative endpoint signs and the \(ze^{-z}=q/e\) equation establish a unique continuous optimizer; finite integer maximizers bracket it, with possible adjacent ties. A standalone independently computed matrix verifier passes all included tests. Numerical tests do not replace analytic quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The closest parameter-dependent source proves bounds for Gaussian sketches and uniform error in an oversampled regime, whereas the claim is an exact nonoversampled two-dimensional stochastic supremum law with a positive maximal-error atom and a sharp independent renewal optimizer. Classical and 2026 sharp randomized-SVD studies concern a single fixed matrix. A prior exact planar pointwise Gaussian mean is explicitly treated as background, not as a new contribution. Specialized unindexed prior covering formulas remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Specialized or unindexed geometric probability results on moving arcs and Gaussian rank-one range sketching may derive an equivalent law; publication priority is not independently confirmed.
The exact benchmark does not extend without additional analysis to adaptive refreshing, higher-rank sketches, or nonmonotone varying singular values.

value.rationale: Constant Gaussian sketches are motivated by computational reuse for smooth parameterized matrix families. The theorem establishes the sharp discrepancy between low expected pointwise error \(O(\varepsilon^{-1})\) and the expected worst-parameter error of order \(\varepsilon^{-2}\) on every positive rotation sweep, gives an exact maximal-error atom, and identifies the globally optimal finite preassigned independent refresh count and equal segmentation. These are precise design-relevant quantities for a natural benchmark, rather than arbitrary tabulation or purely pointwise reformulation.
